body.en: When items can only be ranked (beauty, honesty, preference), or when ranks are easier to compare, use Spearman's *rank correlation*: give each item its rank in each series, find the difference d of the two ranks, and $R = 1 - \dfrac{6\sum d^2}{n(n^2 - 1)}$. Like r, it lies between −1 (rankings reversed) and +1 (identical rankings). Always check that Σd = 0.

points.en: d = difference of the two ranks

say.en: When items can only be ranked (beauty, honesty, preference), or when ranks are easier to compare, use Spearman's rank correlation: give each item its rank in each series, find the difference d of the two ranks, and R equals 1 minus 6 the sum of d squared over (nn squared minus 1). Like r, it lies between minus 1 rankings reversed and plus 1 identical rankings. Always check that Σd equals 0. d equals difference of the two ranks.
R equals 1 minus 6Σd squared/(nn squared minus 1).
Σd equals 0 is a check.

steps.en: Rank the items in the first series.
Rank the same items in the second series.
Find d, the difference of the two ranks of each item, and check Σd = 0.
Square each d and add to get Σd².
